_comment: Measure It reads the lesson prompt aloud only where the lesson's youngest learner is under 8 (internal/readsAloud.ts), so only those prompts are listed; speaksPrompts is false so the recorder does not collect the rest from lessons.json.
The How to play captions are the phrases. Reactions come from the common pack. Must match lessons.json and locales/en.json word for word.
prompts: About how long is it? Pick the one that makes sense.
Draw a line. Start at 0.
Fill the jug to the line.
How heavy is it? Read the scale.
How long is it in inches?
How long is it? Read the ruler.
How many blocks long is it? Lay blocks along it.
How many cubes weigh the same? Make it balance.
How many cups does it fill? Pour it out.
How much does it weigh? Read the scale.
How much does it weigh? Work out the small marks first.
How much longer is one than the other?
How much water is in the jug?
Measure it. Put it on the 0 first.
Put them in order, shortest first.
Start at the first length. Jump. Where do you land?
They cannot move. Use the string to compare them.
This ruler is broken. How long is it?
What temperature does it show?
What would you use to find out? Tap the tool.
Which needs more: cubes or rods?
Which one holds more? Pour each into cups.
Which one is heavier, or lighter? Use the balance.
Which one is longer, or shorter? Tap it.
Which one is really longer? Line them up first.
Which one is taller, or shorter? Tap it.
Which row is measured right? Then count it.
Which unit would you use?
phrases: Which is longer? They must start at the same place.
This one starts late. Tap it.
Now tap the start line.
Both start together now.
This one ends further away. It is longer!
Put them in order, shortest first.
This one is the shortest. Tap it.
Then the middle one.
The longest goes last.
Shortest to longest. Done!
Which is heavier? Use the balance.
Tap to put them on the balance.
This side went down. It is heavier!
Which holds more? Pour each into cups.
Pour the jar into cups.
Now pour the bowl into cups.
The bowl filled more cups. It holds more!
Find the top of the water.
Look across to the marks.
It is on the 300 mark.
How many blocks long is the pencil?
Tap to lay a block.
Lay one after another. No gaps.
It is covered. Count: 1, 2, 3, 4. Four blocks!
How long is the pencil?
Find 0. The pencil starts there.
Look at the end. It ends at 7.
It is 7 cm long.
Measure the crayon.
Tap the crayon to pick it up.
Tap the 0, not the edge.
Now it starts at 0. It ends at 5. It is 5 cm long.
Draw a line 6 cm long.
Tap the 6 mark.
The line goes from 0 to 6. It is 6 cm long.
About how tall is a door?
A door is taller than a grown-up, but not by much.
So a door is about 2 m, not 20 m.
How much does the flour weigh?
Find the number before the needle: 600.
Each small mark is 50 g. 600, then 650.
It weighs 650 g.
What temperature does it show?
Find the top of the red line.
The number below it is 20. Count by 2s: 22, 24, 26.
It is 26 degrees.
A bag has 600 g of flour. A cook uses 250 g.
The whole bar is 600 g. One part is 250 g.
The other part is 600 − 250 = 350 g.
